newsitem.title: USA: Wal-Mart takes stake in Mexico's Cifra.
newsitem.headline: Wal-Mart takes stake in Mexico's Cifra.

text.p: Wal-Mart Stores Inc. said Tuesday it would invest a total of $1.2 billion in its Mexican partner Cifra SA de CV for an eventual 50 percent stake as part of a deal that will combine the two retailers' Mexican joint venture.

Wal-Mart and CIFRA currently operate 145 retail units and restaurants under a joint venture agreement in which each partner has a 50 percent stake. Cifra also operates another 228 retail units and restaurants independently.

The companies said CIFRA will propose to pay $300 million in dividends to all its existing shareholders. Subsequently, the Cifra Wal-Mart joint venture companies will be merged into Cifra, with Wal-Mart receiving shares of Cifra Series A and Series B common stock for its interest in the joint venture.

After the merger is approved by both companies' shareholders, Wal-Mart will make a public tender offer on Mexico's Bolsa Mexicana de Valores for additional Cifra Series A and B voting shares at a price expected to be the peso equivalent of between $1.89 and $2.03.
Wal-Mart's total investment in the tender offer will be approximately $1.2 billion, it said, with the acquired shares representing between 12 percent and 13 percent of Cifra's outstanding shares.
After the merger and tender offer are completed, Wal-Mart expects to own a majority of the voting stock, the companies said in a joint statement.

Cifra, with 50,000 employees, had $2.9 billion in sales for the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 1996, and net earnings of $257 million. Wal-Mart, with more than 675,000 U.S. employess and 50,000 internationally, operates in all 50 states, Argentina, Canada, and Puerto Rico, and in Brazil, China, Indonesia, and Mexico under joint venture or franchise agreements.
Wal-Mart gained 50 cents to $31 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
